10.1d — 2-Button Jam: Playtest

Freeze the build; test the humans. Today is data (9.5's methods on your own game) — deaths per minute, where testers stall, what they say — and the one-fix discipline that turns two hours of testing into two hours of improvement.

Playtest Day ~50 min

Rotation (three rounds):

  1. Round 1 — strangers play (15 min). Swap stations with another team. Silent watching (2.4). Record on the beat table: stall point, death point, the exact QUOTE ("wait, what does that do?"), and the moment of first smile. That smile is your game working.
  2. Round 2 — the one fix (15 min). Each team picks ONE thing from Round 1 data. Apply it. Ship the fix, commit: "10.1d: playtest fix #1".
  3. Round 3 — verify (10 min). New tester (or the same one). Did THAT moment change? If yes: pick fix #2. If no: the fix failed — revert it and write why. One-variable testing (3.4 tuning, jam-scale).

What to watch for in a two-input game specifically:

  • Input confusion: the tester presses the WRONG verb under pressure. That is not tester error — your two verbs are too similar (fix with feel, 6.3: sharper timing or clearer consequence)
  • Button mashing: both verbs at once, always. Your game has one verb wearing two costumes
  • The stall: tester stops playing and asks a question out loud — write the QUESTION down; it is your tutorial, spoken by the void
Close of Day ~5 min

Checkpoint — before moving on, you must be able to:

  • Run three silent playtest rounds and record quotes + numbers
  • Apply one fix, verify it, revert it if it failed
  • Diagnose verb-confusion vs mashing vs stalls and prescribe fixes
  • Ship a playtest.csv into your repo
